heroHeadline: Iran Formally Suspends US Talks; IRGC Threatens Bab el-Mandeb; Trump Picks Pulte as Acting DNI — Day 499
heroSubtitle: On June 2, 2026 (Day 499 of Trump's second term / Day 94 of the US-Iran war), Iran formally suspended all negotiations and message exchanges with the United States via intermediaries. Iranian FM Araghchi declared the ceasefire covers 'all fronts' — Israel's escalating offensive in Lebanon's southern suburbs constitutes a violation that nullifies the broader truce. IRGC Quds Force commander Brigadier General Esmail Qa'ani warned that the Bab al-Mandab Strait — through which approximately 4.7 million barrels of oil transit daily — would face the same traffic restrictions as the Strait of Hormuz if Israel continued operations in Lebanon and Gaza. Trump responded by telling CNBC the talks 'started to get very boring' and he didn't care if they ended, while simultaneously posting on Truth Social that talks are continuing at a 'rapid pace' — and telling ABC News a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is reachable 'over the next week.' A regional source later told CNN that talks appeared back on track hours after Iran's suspension. Brent crude fell to approximately $91-96/bbl on signs of possible resumption (from June 1 spike of ~$104-107/bbl). Trump also named FHFA chief Bill Pulte as acting Director of National Intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who announced her resignation effective June 30 — Pulte has no intelligence background; Sen. Schumer called him 'a partisan thug.' A Big Data Poll (field dates May 24-27) showed Trump below 40% approval (39.4%) for the first time in his second term. Defense Secretary Hegseth blocked at least 7 Navy captain-to-admiral promotions, including women and Black officers. Six-state midterm primaries were held in California, Iowa, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, and South Dakota; Trump endorsed Steve Hilton for the California Republican gubernatorial nomination.
